'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****[[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran]]
******The [[United States Central Command]] launches a new round of strikes against Iran in an effort to degrade capabilities used to attack commercial shipping in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] ahead of the naval blockade. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/iran-strikes-hormuz-strait-blockade-trump-tolls.html (CNBC)]
*****The [[United States]] [[United States Armed Forces|military]] reimposes the [[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran|naval blockade]] of [[Iran]] that ended on June 17 last month in response to ship attacks. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-hormuz-strait-war-july-14-2026-abd060c55feea216625689e57d8f76be (AP)] [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260714-us-military-reimposes-naval-blockade-on-iranian-ports-launches-new-strikes (France 24)]
****[[Iran]] fires projectiles at two [[tanker (ship)|tanker]]s in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] associated with the [[United Arab Emirates]], killing two mariners and injuring 14 others. [https://english.news.cn/europe/20260715/d30044a67ef141559ad18822d01cbffa/c.html (Xinhua)]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] cancels a proposal to implement a 20% fee on cargo ships transiting through the strait. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-hormuz-strait-war-july-14-2026-abd060c55feea216625689e57d8f76be (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8d2vn38dy1o (BBC News)]
***[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[Kuwait]]'s [[Kuwait Armed Forces|military]] says that Iran struck a [[Kuwait Naval Force|navy]] vessel, injuring four personnel, while its [[air defences]] intercept one [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|ballistic missile]], five [[cruise missile]]s, and 33 [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|drones]] aimed at civilian facilities. [https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2650875/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News Pakistan'')]
***Explosions are reported in the Iranian cities of [[Ahvaz]] and [[Bandar Abbas]], and the islands of [[Kish Island|Kish]] and [[Qeshm Island|Qeshm]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/explosions-heard-irans-bandar-abbas (''Middle East Eye'')]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks]]
****The first day of direct negotiations and the sixth round of peace talks between [[Israel]] and [[Lebanon]] begins at the [[Embassy of the United States, Rome|U.S. embassy]] in [[Rome]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/lebanon-israel-conclude-1st-day-of-direct-talks-in-rome/3997967 (AA)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/sixth-round-of-israel-lebanon-talks-begins-in-rome-with-focus-on-idf-pullout-pilot/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israeli military]] strikes a [[Gaza civil police|police]] station in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], killing eight people, according to [[Palestinian Civil Defence|Gaza's civil defence agency]] and [[Al-Shifa Hospital]], violating the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/israel-strike-gaza-police-station-eight-killed-hamas-6254391 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[Iraqi conflict]]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq (2025–2026)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq]]
***[[Iraqi prime minister]] [[Ali al-Zaidi]] and the [[U.S. defense department]] says that all remaining [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] will withdraw from [[Iraq]] by September 30, ending a 23-year presence in the country that started with the [[2003 invasion of Iraq|2003 U.S. invasion]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iraq-trump-islamic-state-group-military-45e64c99d07939951c86308f95dd02ef (AP)] [https://www.dw.com/en/us-troop-withdrawal-from-iraq-set-for-september-30/a-77959648 (DW)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] say that the 4th Infantry Division's 13th Brigade have taken control of the [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] town of Fashfoun following days of clashes with the paramilitary [[Rapid Support Forces]] and the [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]]. [https://www.trtafrika.com/english/article/88c42f10d943 (TRT Afrika)] [https://en.yenisafak.com/world/sudan-army-captures-fashfoun-area-from-rsf-3720818 (''Yeni Şafak'')]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[Colombia]]'s [[Military Forces of Colombia|military]] says it has rescued 39 civilians [[Kidnappings in Colombia|kidnapped]] by the [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]] on a [[Highways in Colombia|highway]] in [[Chocó Department]], with two soldiers killed during the operation. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/07/colombian-military-frees-39-people-kidnapped-by-guerrillas/ (AFP via ''Vanguard'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024–2026 Cuba blackouts]], [[2026 Cuban crisis]]
**[[Cuba]] suffers its third nationwide [[Power outage|blackout]] in less than 10 days and fifth of 2026, as the [[state utility]] reports a complete [[Electrical grid|grid]] failure amid [[Economy of Cuba|fuel shortages]] caused by the ongoing U.S. imposed blockade, that complicate power restoration. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260714-cuba-faces-third-nationwide-blackout-in-less-than-10-days (AFP via RFI)]
*Seven people are killed and three others are injured after two vehicles [[collided head-on]] just outside [[Ramadi]], [[Iraq]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260715/46f073bb27d3492e9c4b24ee980e4cdf/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Six people are killed after a gas-laden truck caught fire and exploded at a checkpoint along a federal highway in [[Kogi State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://punchng.com/six-killed-as-gas-truck-explodes-at-kogi-army-checkpoint/ (The PunchNG)]
*Six workers are killed in a fire at a building under construction in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9323knejyzo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak]]
**The [[Directorate General of Health Services (Bangladesh)|Directorate General of Health Services]] reports that seven more children have died from [[measles]] in [[Bangladesh]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the total death toll from the disease in the country to 766. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/health/measles-related-deaths-rise-766-seven-more-children-die-1488086 (''The Business Standard'')]
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] (DRC) announces that it will test the [[Gilead Sciences]] antiviral for the [[Bundibugyo ebolavirus|Bundibugyo strain]] of the [[Ebola]] [[Ebolavirus|virus]]. [https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/congo-begins-trial-of-gileads-experimental-antiviral-for-ebola-bundibugyo (CNBC Africa)]
**The [[World Health Organization]] reports that 80% of cases of [[Ebola]] in eastern DRC are from unknown chains of transmission. Additionally, the death toll from Ebola reaches 700. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-ebola-outbreak-who-a9093ea39928bfa3f2f0e5aa13c506bb (AP)] 
*[[Cyclosporiasis#2026 United States summer outbreak|2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] reports 7,000 cases [[United States|nationwide]] of [[cyclosporiasis]], which is caused by ''[[cyclospora cayetanensis]]''. [https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/cyclosporiasis-7000-cases-us-cdc-parasite-explosive-diarrhea-rcna587445 (NBC News)]
**The [[Michigan Department of Health and Human Services]] reports 3,300 cases in [[Michigan|the state]], up from 2,640 the previous day. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2026/07/14/michigan-cyclosporiasis-cases-surge-past-3000/90914347007/ (''The Detroit News'')]
